answer.notes: EventSources.processResponse calls RealEventSource.processResponse directly (synchronous path). EventSources.createFactory returns a Factory that constructs RealEventSource and calls connect(client), which enqueues the call; the async Callback.onResponse then delegates to processResponse, so the factory-created EventSource path is also affected. Potential impact only, not a safety proof.

Impact report (status found, no truncation, 23 observed affected) shows two public okhttp3.sse.EventSources entries reaching RealEventSource#processResponse: EventSources.processResponse via a direct bytecode call, and EventSources.createFactory via the private createFactory$lambda-1 -> RealEventSource.connect -> RealCall.enqueue -> Dispatcher/AsyncCall.run -> Callback.onResponse -> RealEventSource.onResponse -> processResponse (asynchronous path; includes a dispatchModel override edge). Potential impact only: limitations include saved-graph freshness, 144/270 files with uncertain index freshness, conservative dispatch candidates and reflection gaps, so external consumers and runtime paths need additional validation. No safety or test-selection conclusions drawn.

processNextEvent() is invoked in the loop inside RealEventSource.processResponse(). EventSources.processResponse calls it synchronously. EventSources.createFactory returns a Factory whose newEventSource path calls RealEventSource.connect(), which enqueues the call asynchronously; the resulting Callback.onResponse delegates to processResponse and thus to processNextEvent on the OkHttp dispatcher thread. Both entry points affect onEvent/onClosed/onFailure listener behavior. This is potential impact only, not a safety proof; based solely on the two files read in the recorded interaction.
